title: fly-proxy sends TCP keepalive probes every ~5 s on idle client connections, costly for cellular IoT
text: We run an MQTT broker on Fly (TCP service on 8883 with handlers = ["tls"] , MQTT keepalive 270 s). Our clients are battery-powered LTE-M devices. The Fly edge sends a zero-length TCP keepalive probe on every idle client connection about every 5.12 s. The first probe comes 2–5 s after the last data. Our app never sees this traffic: the server-side socket shows only the MQTT PINGREQ/PINGRESP every 270 s. Captured on fixed broadband (macOS, idle connection to a Fly app on 66.241.125.92:443): 07:55:24.198873 IP 66.241.125.92.443 > 192.168.1.176.59731: Flags [.], ack 67, win 1024, length 0 07:55:24.199066 IP 192.168.1.176.59731 > 66.241.125.92.443: Flags [.], ack 90, win 2048, length 0 07:55:29.318453 IP 66.241.125.92.443 > 192.168.1.176.59731: Flags [.], ack 67, win 1024, length 0 07:55:29.318634 IP 192.168.1.176.59731 > 66.241.125.92.443: Flags [.], ack 90, win 2048, length 0 07:55:34.438639 IP 66.241.125.92.443 > 192.168.1.176.59731: Flags [.], ack 67, win 1024, length 0 07:55:34.438854 IP 192.168.1.176.59731 > 66.241.125.92.443: Flags [.], ack 90, win 2048, length 0 07:55:39.558423 IP 66.241.125.92.443 > 192.168.1.176.59731: Flags [.], ack 67, win 1024, length 0 A modem trace from the device on 8883 shows the same probe (seq = snd_una − 1, length 0) every 5.12 s for hours. On cellular, every probe pages the device and forces an RRC connection. Measured overnight it costs about 1.4 MB/day per device, more than 40 MB/month of pure keepalive. It also keeps the radio connected about 80 % of the time, which kills battery life. The connection itself is healthy: the device answers every probe. From TCP idle timeouts restrictions have been removed we understand the edge sets SO_KEEPALIVE / TCP_KEEPIDLE / TCP_KEEPINTVL / TCP_KEEPCNT / TCP_USER_TIMEOUT on client sockets. We couldn’t find these values or any setting for them in the docs. Questions: Is ~5 s really the intended TCP_KEEPIDLE/TCP_KEEPINTVL for client-side edge connections? Can it be raised (e.g. ≥ 300 s) or disabled per app or per service, for example as an option under [[services.ports]] ? The application already has its own keepalive. If not, what is the recommended way to serve long-lived, mostly idle TCP connections to cellular clients on Fly? Thanks! 3 posts - 2 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Developer experiencing costly TCP keepalive probes disrupting IoT devices.

title: Feature Request: Customizable @-Mention Search Priorities and Preferred Tables
text: Feature Request: Allow users to customize @-mention search priorities Problem When using @-mentions in Superhuman Docs (formerly Coda), search results are presented in a predefined order, with people and pages frequently appearing before table rows. For users who rely extensively on table-based references within their documents, this creates unnecessary friction and significantly reduces the efficiency of the writing experience. Use case I maintain a centralized glossary (ABC) in a dedicated table within my document. This table contains terminology and definitions used throughout our internal policies and procedures. While writing these documents, I frequently insert @-mentions referencing specific glossary entries. This functionality is particularly valuable because readers can hover over a referenced term to view its definition without leaving the document. However, when I type something like @b , the search results initially show numerous colleagues and pages before eventually displaying relevant entries from my glossary. Finding the correct reference can require extensive scrolling or typing additional characters, interrupting the writing process. Suggested improvement Allow users to customize the search behavior and priority of @-mentions. Ideally, this would include: Customizable result priorities: Allow users to determine whether people, pages, tables, or table rows should appear first. Preferred tables: Allow users to designate specific tables as preferred sources for @-mentions. Contextual search: Introduce an option to search directly within a specific table, for example by using a syntax such as @ABC:term . Persistent preferences: Remember these preferences at the user or document level. Why this matters One of the key strengths of Superhuman Docs is the ability to combine structured data with traditional document editing. Using table rows as inline references creates powerful opportunities for interactive documentation, particularly for policy manuals, compliance frameworks, knowledge bases, and internal procedures. However, the current search behavior makes this functionality unnecessarily cumbersome. Workarounds such as manually copying row links or navigating back and forth between pages defeat the purpose of having an efficient inline referencing system. Expected benefit Giving users control over @-mention search priorities would significantly improve the writing experience, especially for organizations using Superhuman Docs as a centralized knowledge management and documentation platform. Even a relatively simple option to prioritize one or more specific tables would already make a substantial difference. 1 post - 1 participant Read full topic
triage_reason: User experiencing friction and inefficiency with search priorities in docs.

title: High power drain when suspended due to ACPI table, with workaround
text: Framework Laptop 12 (13th Gen Intel): s2idle never reaches S0ix on Linux because BIOS sets STD3=1, keeping the NVMe root port (PEG0) in D0 This report and debug process are AI-aided. I have no deep understanding of ACPI/BIOS/firmware/Linux kernel. Related code and debug helpers, including the workaround kernel module, are on GitHub at GitHub - Ronmi/fw12-s0ix-debug · GitHub (written in Traditional Chinese). The module is a proof of concept for this report, not a recommended fix; use it at your own risk. Summary On the Framework Laptop 12 (13th Gen Intel Core), s2idle on Linux never reaches S0ix : the CPU package never goes deeper than PC3, and the battery drains about 3–5 %/hour while suspended (about 30 % overnight). The cause is in the firmware’s ACPI tables. The GNVS variable STD3 is 1 (Storage D3 enabled, but not RTD3). \_SB.PC00.PEG0._INI copies it into PEG0.RD3C , and with RD3C != 2 : PEG0._S0W returns 0 (D0) , so the OS must keep the CPU PCIe root port of the NVMe SSD (00:06.0) in D0 during s2idle, and PEG0.GPRS returns 0, so the PXP power resource _OFF / _ON are no-ops. When RD3C is forced to 2 at runtime, everything else stays the same and the firmware’s own RTD3 path works perfectly. The root port and the SSD go to D3cold, the package reaches PC10, the system spends 99.8 % of suspend time in S0i3.0 , and drain drops to about 1 %/hour . Resume is reliable. System Item Value Model Framework Laptop 12 (13th Gen Intel Core), board FRAPMACP05 rev A5 CPU Intel Core i5-1334U (Raptor Lake-U) BIOS 03.07 (02/10/2026), 03.08 (08/20/2026) and 03.09 — all affected SSD Kingston NV3 2230 (SNV3SM31T0, SM2268XT2, DRAM-less, HMB), firmware SDX01100 OS Debian 13, Linux 7.1.13 (backports) and 7.2.6 Sleep mode s2idle (default; deep is also offered) Symptoms /sys/kernel/debug/pmc_core/slp_s0_residency_usec and the S0i2.0/S0i3.0 substate residencies stay at 0 after every suspend. With intel_pmc_core.warn_on_s0ix_failures=1 , the kernel reports CPU did not enter Package C10!!! on every resume. Package C6–C10 counters stay at 0, and only PC2/PC3 increase. There are no spurious wakeups; the only wake event is the lid (EC GPE, IRQ 9). Intel’s S0ixSelftestTool reports: “Your system achieved PC3 residency, but no PC8 residency during S2idle” . It also reports that pcieport 0000:00:06.0 stays in D0 ( PCI PM: Skipped ) and that its link is only in L1, not L1.1/L1.2. Analysis Firmware logic (from SSDT “SaSsdt” and SSDT “ADL-P-M”, BIOS 03.08) SSDT SaSsdt (rev 0x3000), \_SB.PC00.PEG0._INI : If ((\_SB.PC00.PEG0.PEGP.PNVM () || \_SB.PC00.PEG0.PEGP.PAHC ())) { \_SB.PC00.PEG0.RD3C = \STD3 } SSDT ADL-P-M , \_SB.PC00.PEG0 : Method (_S0W, 0, NotSerialized) { If (CondRefOf (RD3C)) { If ((RD3C == 0x02)) { Return (0x04) } } Return (Zero) // D0 } Method (GPRS, 0, NotSerialized) // gate used by PXP._ON/_OFF { ... If (CondRefOf (RD3C)) { If ((RD3C != 0x02)) { Return (Zero) } } ... Return (One) } \_SB.PC00.PEG0.PEGP._S0W similarly returns 3 (D3hot) instead of 4 when RD3C != 2 . Since STD3 != 0 , PEGP._DSD still exposes StorageD3Enable = 1 , so Linux puts the SSD into D3hot (“simple suspend”). However, the root port is not allowed below D0. On Linux, for S0 the _S0W limit is applied whenever the device has _PRW , regardless of the user’s wakeup setting. Runtime values (read from GNVS at 0x448F9018 on BIOS 03.08) Variable Value Meaning OSYS 0x07DF sanity check (Windows 2015 _OSI ) STD3 1 Storage D3 only, not RTD3 SD2P / SDP1 0x0908000E / 1 SSD power-enable GPIO pad, active high SD2R / SDR1 0x090C0014 / 0 SSD reset (PERST#) GPIO pad, active low PEP0 100 power-on delay (ms) The RTD3 GPIOs are configured , so the hardware path is clearly wired. Only the STD3 value keeps it disabled. Kernel trace confirming the D-state decision A kprobe on acpi_pm_device_sleep_state() during suspend (stock BIOS tables): dev="0000:00:06.0" ret=0 # root port: firmware allows D0 only dev="0000:01:00.0" ret=3 # NVMe: D3hot only With RD3C = 2 : dev="0000:00:06.0" ret=4 # D3cold dev="0000:01:
triage_reason: Laptop user experiencing high power drain during suspend mode on Linux.

title: What is your stock worth? The answer turns on what your tool does with the units that have no cost on them
text: You want one number: what the stock on the shelf is worth at cost. Shopify holds the quantities and it holds a cost per item field, but it never multiplies the two for you, so the number comes from somewhere else - a report, an app, or a spreadsheet. Wherever it comes from, it has to decide something first, and it rarely tells you what it decided. A real shop has variants with the cost field empty. Three things can happen to those units. They can be counted as costing nothing. The total still looks authoritative, it is just smaller than the truth, and nothing on the screen says so. They can be dropped instead, which produces the same quietly smaller number for a different reason. Or they can be counted as units that cannot be valued, and reported beside the figure. The first two give you a number that is wrong in a direction you cannot see, and that is the number that goes to an accountant. The check takes a minute on your own setup. Find a variant with cost per item empty and some stock on hand, note your valuation total, fill the cost in, and look again. If the total jumps by more than that one product’s worth, something had been counting other empty ones as free too. What I would like to know from people actually doing this: what share of your variants have a cost on them at all? And when the year-end number goes to your accountant, does anyone reconcile it against anything, or does it go as it comes out? 3 posts - 3 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Merchant dealing with missing cost data issues during inventory valuation.

title: Feature request: Option to retain retail compare-at prices in discounted catalogs
text: We operate a Shopify Plus store with a lot of B2B customers. When we sign up a B2B customer and allocate them a discounted catalog, they have no indication that their pricing has been discounted. Because the discount is not displayed, they assume they are not being offered the discount they were promised. The current implementation: When you create a discounted catalog, there is an option to include compare-at price . The way this works is that the compare-at field of the catalog is also automatically populated from basic retail pricing, and the compare-at field is also discounted like the price field. The effect is that existing retail discounts are carried over to the catalog, which does have it’s use case. But non-discounted products display with the reduced price, but no indication that it is reduced from retail pricing. Our suggestion: We want an additional switch, shown when include compare-at price is on, to control adjust compare-at price . If this new switch is on (on by default) then the existing behaviour is retained and the compare-at price is also reduced. If this switch is off, then then retail compare-at price is carried over to the catalog without any adjustment. The effect is that all products in the catalog show up with a discount. Reasoning: Discounting is a powerful way of making customers feel satisfied. Our B2B program is intended to encourage long-term support from our customers, and making their savings visible will be a significant advantage. 7 posts - 4 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Merchant struggling with B2B customers not seeing discounted pricing tiers.

title: Feature Request: Option to skip Time Logs in Job Card per Operation (Work Order / BOM)
text: Summary Add a checkbox “Skip Time Logs” (Yes/No) on the Operation (and/or BOM Operation / Work Order Operation) so that Job Cards for that operation can be submitted without entering time logs. Problem When a BOM has “With Operations” enabled, the Work Order creates Job Cards for each operation. On submit, ERPNext requires at least one time log: “Time logs are required for Job Card …” For many small manufacturers, operators do not track start/end time for every operation. They only need to confirm that the operation is done and record the completed quantity. Entering dummy time logs every time is extra work and gives wrong time data. Current Workaround We use a Server Script (Job Card, Before Submit) that adds a time log automatically using the planned time (time_required) from the BOM operation. This works, but it is a workaround, and every company has to build it themselves. Proposed Solution Add a checkbox “Skip Time Logs” in: Operation master (default for that operation), and/or BOM Operation row, copied to Work Order Operation If checked, the Job Card: Can be submitted with an empty Time Logs table Uses Completed Qty entered directly on the Job Card Uses planned time (time_required) for Work Order actual time and operating cost, or leaves it as planned If unchecked, keep the current behaviour (time logs mandatory). Benefits Simpler shop-floor process for operations where time tracking is not needed No dummy or incorrect time data Still keeps operation-wise progress tracking through Job Cards Version ERPNext: v16 Frappe: v16 5 posts - 4 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Small manufacturer needing to skip time logs for specific operations.
